named capture group.description:
(?<name>pattern)
named capture groups let you reference a match by a name instead of an index, via `match.groups.name`.

lookbehind assertion.description:
(?<=pattern) positive lookbehind, (?<!pattern) negative lookbehind
asserts what precedes the match without including it in the result.

/pattern/d (match indices).description:
ES2022
the `d` flag makes `exec()`/`matchAll()` results include an `indices` property with `[start, end]` positions for the whole match and each capture group.

/pattern/v (unicode sets).description:
ES2024
the `v` flag is an upgrade to `u` (unicode) mode, adding set notation and string properties inside character classes — e.g. `[\\p{RGI_Emoji}]` or `[[a-z]--[aeiou]]`. Mutually exclusive with the `u` flag.

RegExp.escape().description:
ES2025
RegExp.escape(string)
return a new string with all regex-syntax characters escaped, safe to interpolate into a `RegExp` pattern. Prefer this over hand-rolled escaping when building a dynamic pattern from user input.

RegExp.prototype.exec().description:
Syntax: regexp.exec(str)
executes a search for a match in a specified string.
return a result array, or **null**.

RegExp.prototype.test().description:
Syntax: regexp.test(str)
executes a search for a match between a regular expression and a specified string. 
return **true** or **false**.

get RegExp[@@species].description:
ES2015
Syntax: RegExp[Symbol.species]
The RegExp[@@species] accessor property returns the RegExp constructor.

RegExp.prototype[@@match]().description:
ES2015
Syntax: regexp[Symbol.match](str)
The [@@match]() method retrieves the matches when matching a string against a regular expression.

RegExp.prototype[@@matchAll]().description:
ES2015
Syntax: regexp[Symbol.matchAll](str)
The [@@matchAll] method returns all matches of the regular expression against a string.

RegExp.prototype[@@replace]().description:
ES2015
Syntax: regexp[Symbol.replace](str, newSubStr|function)
The [@@replace]() method replaces some or all matches of a this pattern in a string by a replacement, and returns the result of the replacement as a new string. The replacement can be a string or a function to be called for each match.

RegExp.prototype[@@search]().description:
ES2015
Syntax: regexp[Symbol.search](str)
The [@@search]() method executes a search for a match between a this regular expression and a string.

RegExp.prototype[@@split]().description:
ES2015
Syntax: regexp[Symbol.split](str[, limit])
The [@@split]() method splits a String object into an array of strings by separating the string into substrings.
